title: Castle of Good Hope named among South Africa's most haunted places
excerpt: A PlayCasino analysis of 34 published lists found that the Castle of Good Hope and Nottingham Road Hotel were the most frequently cited reportedly haunted places in South Africa
content:
The Castle of Good Hope in Cape Town is among the places most often named as haunted in South Africa.Picture: Tracey Adams / Independent Newspapers

The Castle of Good Hope has been named among South Africa’s most haunted places, according to a new analysis of published ghost stories and guides.

The Cape Town landmark ranked joint first with the Nottingham Road Hotel in KwaZulu-Natal, with both places appearing in 13 of 15 publishers’ lists of reportedly haunted locations.

The analysis, conducted by PlayCasino, looked at 34 published lists and guides from 15 different publishers and recorded how often each location was named.

More than 50 places appeared at least once.

The Castle of Good Hope

Built between 1666 and 1679, the Castle of Good Hope is the oldest surviving colonial building in South Africa.

Among the legends associated with the Castle is the ghost of Pieter Gysbert van Noodt, an 18th-century governor who is said to have died on the same day he refused the final wish of a condemned man.

Another reported sighting involves a large black dog which allegedly appears inside the Castle before disappearing.

The stories surrounding the Castle have helped cement its reputation as one of Cape Town’s best-known supposedly haunted sites.

The Castle is not the only Western Cape location high on the list.

Other haunted places making the list

The Uniondale ghost road and Lord Milner Hotel in Matjiesfontein ranked joint third, each appearing in 11 publishers’ lists.

The Uniondale legend centres on a hitchhiker who is said to appear on the road before mysteriously disappearing from a vehicle. The story has been linked to Maria Charlotte Roux, who died in a car crash on the road in 1968.

At the Lord Milner Hotel, which dates back to 1899, one of the best-known ghost stories involves Kate, a young nurse who is reportedly heard shuffling playing cards.

Further down the list, the Flying Dutchman at Cape Point and Kimberley’s Africana Library were each named by nine publishers.

The Flying Dutchman is the legendary ghost ship said to have been lost in a storm off the Cape in 1641, while the Africana Library is reportedly haunted by its first qualified librarian, Bertrand Dyer.

South Africa’s most frequently named haunted places

  1. Castle of Good Hope, Cape Town – 13 publishers
  2. Nottingham Road Hotel, KwaZulu-Natal Midlands – 13
  3. Uniondale Ghost Road, Western Cape – 11
  4. Lord Milner Hotel, Matjiesfontein – 11
  5. Flying Dutchman, Cape Point – 9
  6. Africana Library, Kimberley – 9
  7. Tokai Manor House, Cape Town – 7
  8. Kempton Park Hospital, Gauteng – 7
  9. The Old Gaol, Makhanda – 7
  10. Smuts House, Irene – 5
  11. Victoria Hotel, Pretoria – 5

Five of the locations in the top 10 are in the Western Cape.

The ranking is based on how frequently places are described as haunted, rather than evidence that they are actually haunted. The analysis also notes that each publisher was counted once per location, regardless of how many times that publisher had featured the site.

The data experts at playcasino.com said: "Every town has a ghost story, so we wanted to see which ones the whole country seems to agree on.

The Castle and the Nottingham Road Hotel came up again and again, and you can see why. They're old, you can still walk into both of them, and the stories have been told for generations. We're not saying any of these places is haunted. We're saying these are the ones South Africans keep coming back to."

So, whether you believe in ghosts or not, the Castle has clearly earned its place in South Africa’s haunted folklore.
